sources.title: competition brochure 1
sources.note: Competition brochure cover and exhibition information. Establishes the event and sponsors.

sources.title: competition brochure 2
sources.note: Competition award list and winning alphabets. Best primary check of names and award wording.

sources.title: competition advert 1
sources.note: Four Irish Typefaces sales flyer: all four alphabets, alternates, figures, marks, sheet codes and sizes. Same layout as the repository source.

sources.title: competition advert 2
sources.note: Large Carrick and Kilfane specimens. Kilfane shares blemishes with N516: useful additional reproduction, not an independent master.

sources.title: Carrick alphabet specimen
sources.note: Carrick alphabet specimen. Compare shape structure and counters; the catalogue does not establish this digital image as original outline artwork.

sources.title: Carrick Letraset
sources.note: Photograph of Carrick transfer sheets. Repeated letters help distinguish recurring forms from damage. Sheets overlap and some content is cropped.

sources.title: Kilfane alphabet specimen
sources.note: Kilfane alphabet and alternates; not established as a drawing master. Correlated reproduction history with N47.

sources.title: Kilfane Letraset
sources.note: Photograph of Kilfane transfer sheets. Repeated letters and alternative capitals; perspective, overlap and cropping limit direct measurement.

sources.title: Mary Ann Bolger, Designing Modern Ireland (2017), volume 1
sources.note: Printed pp. 278–280: competition context and sources; 73 entries, 24 exhibited. Footnotes provide archival and family research leads.

sources.title: Mary Ann Bolger (2017), volume 2: illustrations
sources.note: PDF pp. 157–164, figures 201–206: competition ephemera, 1974 book cover, Tuam development work and complete transfer sheet.

sources.title: Della Varrilly, Irish-English Bilingualism and its Relation to Graphic Design (1982)
sources.note: PDF pp. 94, 96, 98: figures 30–34 show Calli, Carrick, Tuam, Armóin and Kilfane. Printed pp. 73–76 discuss them. Near-contemporary criticism is opinion, not a redesign specification.

sources.title: Una O’Shea, An Irish Identity as Expressed Through Contemporary Graphic Design (1993)
sources.note: PDF p. 74, figure 23: another reproduction of competition alphabets. Useful corroboration; weaker outline evidence than the archive scans.

sources.title: Eimear O’Keane, The Role of Design in the Revival of the Irish Language (2022)
sources.note: PDF pp. 32–33 discuss Tuam and modern Irish design. Contextual secondary source; do not use its compressed chronology to date the original production.

sources.title: Signal Type Foundry: Jarlath specimen
sources.note: Modern revival material. Recorded only to disambiguate historical sources; excluded from reconstruction and outline comparison.

sources.title: Gaelchló: Caolchló GC specimen
sources.note: Modern revival material. Recorded only to disambiguate historical sources; excluded from reconstruction and outline comparison.

sources.title: Klingspor Museum: Jarlath Hayes
sources.note: Short designer reference and specimen; its early date should be kept distinct from the confirmed 1978 competition.

sources.title: Heritage Outlook, summer 2011
sources.note: Printed p. 37: KDW archive context and the 1978 competition poster; useful for following the archive trail.

sources.title: NIVAL: William Curran Archive
sources.note: Primary archive overview; Curran biography, both typefaces, banknote use and access to material not all online.

sources.title: NIVAL special collections
sources.note: Further institutional trail: Kilkenny Design Workshops and Dolmen Press collections.

sources.title: NIVAL reproduction policy
sources.note: Reference for obtaining additional scans and publishing collection images. Access does not assign copyright.

sources.title: NIVAL contact
sources.note: Public research contact: nivalinfo@ncad.ie; arrange a reading-room visit or ask about scans.

sources.title: Signal Type Foundry: Jarlath
sources.note: Designer’s own account explicitly describes changes to Tuam’s squareness, contrast and spacing, plus new styles.

sources.title: Gaelchló: Caolchló GC
sources.note: Released in 2025, based on Hecht’s design; explicitly removes i/j dots and lowers insular s. Provides OpenType/WOFF downloads and stylistic sets.

sources.title: Caolchló GC character map
sources.note: Modern revival material. Recorded only to disambiguate historical sources; excluded from reconstruction and outline comparison.

sources.title: Gaelchló usage information
sources.note: Consult published usage and modification terms before using modern font software; it is not a source of unrestricted original outlines.

sources.title: Dublin Inquirer: Irish font brought into the digital age (24 June 2020)
sources.note: Interviews concerning Hayes, Susan Waine and Max Phillips. Useful evidence that the revival project predates its later retail listing.

sources.title: Irish Times: Master typographer and designer (2001)
sources.note: Hayes obituary; biographical and usage context, not a tracing source.

sources.title: 100 Archive: Zoe (2021)
sources.note: Documents use of Jarlath beta in a design project.

sources.title: Fonts In Use: Céili
sources.note: Links to Design no. 357 and reports NLI booklet/Glenroe use. Those applications need object-level confirmation.

sources.title: Fonts In Use: Kilfane
sources.note: Links back to NIVAL. Its 1973 release date is not established by sheet boilerplate alone.

sources.title: ATypI: ReTyping Europe
sources.note: Scholarly framing of modern Irish typography and transnational heritage.

sources.title: National Print Museum: Irish Type Design, Dermot McGuinne
sources.note: Second edition, 2010. Authoritative broader history; its relevance to specific missing 1978 glyphs still needs inspection.

sources.title: Central Bank of Ireland: Series C banknotes
sources.note: Primary source for banknote applications associated with Kilfane. Verify any adaptations before treating lettering as font outlines.

sources.title: Microsoft OpenType: stylistic-set features
sources.note: Technical reference for preserving alternate glyphs in ss01–ss20.

sources.title: W3C: WOFF File Format 2.0
sources.note: Technical reference for web delivery; changing the wrapper does not improve outline fidelity.

sources.title: ddrayne/four-irish-typefaces
sources.note: Release 2.000 is the baseline. Subsequent Kilfane research is isolated in research/kilfane-study-01; see HANDOFF.md.

sources.title: Design magazine, no. 357, September 1978
sources.note: Contemporary report/glyph-set lead linked by Fonts In Use. Archive metadata located, but PDF and JP2 files are marked private. Page content was not inspected.

sources.title: Athbheochan: Type Revival and Ideas of Irishness
sources.note: Max Phillips/Mary Ann Bolger event lead from the repository. Page returned 403 during this pass; no recording acquired.

sources.title: Yale finding aid AOB 55
sources.note: Box 5 lists New Letraset Typefaces 1978. Whether it contains these four faces is unverified; lower-priority physical catalogue lead.

sources.title: Screen Archive South East: Hecht Collection
sources.note: Verified magic-lantern collection. It does not establish custody of Céilí drawings. The repository’s V&A claim remains unverified.
